statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-70186 (GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in Kestrel (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core): an unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences that deadlock connection handling and exhaust server resources. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69797, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll at its own .NET version, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and the ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70186 (GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in Kestrel (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core): an unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences that deadlock connection handling and exhaust server resources. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll at its own .NET version, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, plus reference assemblies with no implementation code (including 6.0.2 reference assemblies in source-build reference packages): 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 in the first seven builds and 8.0.32 or later from 8.0.32-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70186 (GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue: crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences can deadlock Kestrel connection handling and exhaust server resources. Microsoft lists the Linux ASP.NET Core runtime packs among the affected packages and fixed .NET 9 in 9.0.21 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: the ASP.NET Core shared framework ships in aspnetcore9-runtime, with further copies in the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in ASP.NET Core NuGet packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts. In every build and on both architectures, the copies of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll, which holds Kestrel's HTTP/3 connection handling, in the ASP.NET Core shared frameworks, the runtime pack and the reference packs carry that build's ASP.NET Core version, as does the shared framework directory; the only copies at another version are metadata-only reference assemblies from the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref 6.0.2 and 8.0.0 reference packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, which hold no code. The copies at the build's version also carry the dotnet/dotnet source commit they were built from: in 9.0.20-r0 it is the v9.0.121 tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.121), which builds ASP.NET Core 9.0.20, and in 9.0.21-r0 it is the v9.0.122 tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.122), which builds ASP.NET Core 9.0.21 and is the first to contain Microsoft's fix, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/4919ba0124e081fd33e5bd66e825efb4f285509b (Fix h3 connection-level and stream-level abort locking), the only change to Kestrel's HTTP/3 code between ASP.NET Core 9.0.20 and 9.0.21. In 9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.20-r0 ASP.NET Core is 9.0.12 through 9.0.20, which are affected; from 9.0.21-r0 on, the version is 9.0.21 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.21-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
